However, the 2026-07-25 batch (R2,359,696 / 9,451 subscriptions) is ~3.4x the equivalent 2026-06-25 run (R689,620) and ~3.6x the 2026-05-25 run (R661,844). This isn't an order-of-magnitude anomaly (not excluded), but the multiple is unusual and worth data-team confirmation — it is currently masking the qty decline in the MTD value comparison.

The qty decline (yesterday, MTD, 3-month trend) is not explained by a pipeline lag — UCONNECT_MAY_MERGE_REVENUE's MAX(TRANSACTION_DATE) is 2026-07-30, ahead of the run_date, so this table is current. This reads as a genuine, sustained decline in transaction volume distinct from the Cell C Recharges pipeline stall above — worth cross-checking against the Telco dashboard and confirming whether it shares a root cause.

21,130 terminations MTD is below the (avg of last 2 months + 500) threshold of 40,907 — avg of 55,429 and 25,384 = 40,407.

MAJOR data-shape event, read the RED flag above with this caveat: the June (prior-MTD, through 06-27) termination figure jumped from 18,255 (as observed in the 2026-07-22 run) to 55,429 (this run) — a 37,174 increase — even though the FULL calendar month of June total is essentially unchanged (72,485 previously vs 72,483 now). This means existing June-terminated records had their TERMINATION_DATE reassigned/corrected to earlier days within the month between the two runs, not that new terminations were added. This is the same 'batch-applied termination dates' issue previously flagged for May, now recurring for June, and it artificially inflates this run's baseline — so the RED flag above may reflect a distorted, inflated baseline rather than a genuine slowdown in July termination processing. Recommend confirming with the data team whether this was an intentional backfill/correction before acting on this flag.

Known data-shape issue, still unresolved: termination dates continue to look batch-applied/subject to retroactive correction within a month rather than flowing evenly day-by-day, as evidenced again by this run's June reshuffle. A day-of-month-cutoff MTD comparison, which works fine for recharges/sales, remains an unreliable read on this metric. Recommend escalating to the data team as a recurring, unresolved data-quality issue rather than continuing to re-flag it each run.
